assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a general, originality-rich method that reshaped how amines and arylamines are made, with enormous use in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and materials. Lasting impact is exceptionally clear and the mechanistic framework (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination, ligand design) is well understood. Cross-coupling was recognised in 2010, but this is a distinct bond-forming method rather than a duplicate.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled, general catalytic systems that made the reaction broadly practical. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor but not the enabling general method, so a two-person prize is defensible; precedence of Migita/Kosugi may be raised.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent use, industrial adoption and mechanistic confirmation; recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Outside my own field, so I weigh it on breadth of impact rather than technical detail.
Treatment of Kosugi/Migita precursor credit is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silica (M41S) opened a new size regime of porous crystalline-like materials beyond zeolites and seeded a large field of mesostructured oxides, carbons and supports. For me this is a core porous-materials story: designed architecture, tunable pores, real catalytic and adsorption applications. Importantly the structures were established by diffraction, TEM and later electron crystallography.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil) made the original discovery; Ryoo extended it to controlled mesoporous carbons and framework/pore engineering; Stucky and Zhao contributed SBA-15 and wide generalisation, and Kuroda/Inagaki-type parallel work is only partially captured. The three-name limit forces a hard allocation and the selection of Ryoo over Stucky or Zhao is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Discovered in 1992; thirty years of independent confirmation, so it is mature. Some may argue the application impact is less than for zeolites, and the delayed recognition risks the field being seen as past its peak.
uncertainties: Credit split between Mobil discoverers and academic extenders is contested.
Industrial impact is more modest than the scientific impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar efficiency from about 4 percent to above 25 percent in little over a decade, a remarkable materials-chemistry story linking composition, crystal structure and optoelectronic function. Impact on the field and on energy research is very large and still growing.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites in sensitised cells, Park delivered the first stable solid-state device, and Snaith established the meso-superstructured and planar thin-film architectures. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also made major contributions, so the three-person limit leaves out important people and the Kojima/Miyasaka initial credit and later contributors are partly contentious.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency record and basic physics are replicated everywhere, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial scale-up remain open, so recognition could be seen as somewhat early.
uncertainties: Device stability and commercial viability are unresolved.
Credit allocation among six names is unclear; the Grätzel link to dye-sensitised cells may be considered a competing story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase structure and mechanism is a fundamental chemistry problem: how a FeMo cofactor with an interstitial carbide reduces N2. The crystallographic work set the foundation of the field and the structural evidence is central; I would insist the cofactor structure, not only the biochemistry, is determined. The significance for nitrogen fixation is obvious.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first FeMo-protein structure and the later cofactor refinements, Einsle identified the central carbide with high-resolution data, Seefeldt and Dean built the mechanistic and biochemical framework, and Ribbe the cofactor biosynthesis. The allocation is the principal difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The structures are well confirmed, but the detailed catalytic mechanism (E4 state, substrate binding site) is still debated, so a prize for mechanism may be premature while structure alone is mature.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 binding still not settled.
Allocation among five or more contributors is hard; a structure-only citation may be preferable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics put electronic structure into dynamics, enabling first-principles study of liquids, interfaces, defects and solids. It changed how materials and condensed-phase chemistry are simulated and is the foundation of ab initio MD codes. The idea is original and clear.
assessment.attribution: The method was set out in a single 1985 paper by two authors, giving an unusually clean credit configuration. Overlap with Parrinello's other candidacies (metadynamics, machine-learned potentials) may offer a broader citation.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, thoroughly confirmed and mature; timely or arguably long overdue.
uncertainties: Committee may prefer a broader award in simulation that combines it with machine-learned potentials.
I am not a computational specialist and rely on colleagues for a field comparison.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base into another without double-strand breaks, a distinct chemical concept built on engineered deaminases fused to Cas proteins. It enabled precise correction of point mutations and has entered clinical use, so the impact is high and rising.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the design of cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead first authors of the key papers. Nishida and Kondo made a parallel cytidine deaminase editor and have a priority claim. Any prize also faces the proximity to the 2020 CRISPR award.
assessment.maturity: Clinical evidence is emerging and off-target and long-term safety data are still maturing, so it might be slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether trainees (Komor, Gaudelli) are suitable laureates versus Liu alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at XFELs lets structures be determined from micro- and nanocrystals and time-resolved at room temperature, using the diffract-before-destroy principle. As a person working on structure from tiny crystals, I value the enabling method highly; it shares my interest in beating crystal-size limits.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof-of-principle experiments and theory, Fromme and Schlichting developed sample delivery and biological applications, and Hajdu proposed the concept of imaging single biomolecules with XFELs. Choosing three of four involves a precedence dispute.
assessment.maturity: The method is established and applied widely, but the number of high-impact new discoveries is still developing and it is tied to scarce facilities, so it is moderately mature.
uncertainties: Hajdu omission and credit dispute with Chapman.
Facility dependence limits community-wide impact compared to routine crystallography.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts, through organic structure-directing agents, new framework topologies, and placement of active sites, links synthesis to structure to shape-selective function. This is the part of porous-materials chemistry I know best: the architecture determines the catalysis and the applications (refining, emissions control such as small-pore Cu-CHA, fine chemicals) are large.
assessment.attribution: Zones (SSZ-13 and structure-directing-agent design at Chevron), Davis (new framework types and catalyst design) and Corma (zeolite catalysis, active-site engineering, ITQ materials) are central. Yu and Tsapatsis are also credible; credit is spread across many groups and new frameworks were often solved by diffraction and electron crystallography by others, so a clean decisive set is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Mature with decades of industrial and academic confirmation; the risk is that it is seen as incremental accumulation rather than one discovery.
uncertainties: The discovery is a broad field rather than a single decisive advance.
Credit is diffuse and Corma, Davis and Zones are not obviously decisive over others.
